title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: I received a few lines from thee, when on your return home from these parts, which were very acceptable to me, being desirous to hear more particular how you fared, as well as how your families fared in your absence, we have not had opportunities as I expected to send & here from your parts, but I hope when there is, it may not be missed for it is a great comfort to me, in my lonesome situation to have an account from my near & dear friends for so you feel to me.

I may with thankfulness acknowledge the many favors bestowed upon us poor unworthy creatures, many ways & in particular, that we are favored with health, (although it has been very changeable weather) & several have been taken away by death as William Wilson’s son William a hopeful young man – Thomas Newport a friend that lives near us, went over the mountain (with Issac Jinkonson) was took with the smallpox had it smartly before he could return to his family. His wife was delivered of twins & she with one of the children is dead, the other like to live, a trying circumstance.

I have thought that your coming to see us, has been of considerable service to me & I believe it has to others feeling myself it times better reconciled to my situation, but oh, the surfeiting cares & cumbering things of this life are many indeed,
that at times I am ready to say in my heart except the Lord help, vain is the help of man, yet have thought I have need of their prayers for me & family that we may be united by the holy sement, which will bring all into order & keep it so: that corrupt unmortified self, may be kept down, I think that Thomas French has been favored with that which has kept self down in a good degree, but, I fear that will not always be the the case, O, I Daily feel the need of wisdom, that, which is profitable to direct inwardly & outwardly that whilst, we are necessary providing for the body, that the more needful part be not neglected, O, I may say in truth that there is breathing in my heart that we may give all diligence to make our calling & election sure, yet feel my weakness & poverty so great that I am unable to do anything; except it is at times in secret petitions.

I believe that it will not be best for me to write to several of any friend as I should be glad to, but don't wish to burden the carrier, therefore if thee will please to remember my kind love to my friends & relations, brother Samuel particular my children joining me in love to thee, thy wife & children
I have wrote thee this poor letter as it came, without considering much how it would read, having my child in my lap whilst the rest are asleep

postscript.label: P.S.
postscript.p: our horses are not all well yet. We have made about one hundred and fifty weight of sugar besides molasses Jonas’ family in a middling state of health
